# Go Green Restoration TX Inc — Company and Service Reference

> Property restoration support in Dallas, Collin County and the wider Dallas–Fort Worth area, based in Wylie, Texas.

Updated October 4, 2026. This reference summarizes the Texas website and links to its service information.

- Website: https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/
- Company: Go Green Restoration TX Inc
- Phone: (469) 727-3217
- Email: info@gogreenrestorationtx.com
- Confirmed location: 611 S State Hwy 78, Suite 133B, Wylie, TX 75098
- Service coverage: Dallas–Fort Worth, with a focus on Dallas and Collin County. City service pages describe coverage from Wylie, not additional offices.
- Emergency calls: accepted 24/7. Call to confirm crew availability and arrival time for the property. Office visiting hours are not specified in this reference.

## Mold service scope

Go Green Restoration TX Inc welcomes mold projects of any size. While our Texas mold remediation license application is pending, work requiring a license is referred to appropriately licensed partner companies. The provider and scope of work are identified before work begins. Independent assessment and clearance are separate services.

## Services

- [Water Damage Restoration](https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/services/water-damage-restoration/): Discuss water extraction, structural drying, affected materials and the handoff to repairs.
- [Fire & Smoke Damage Restoration](https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/services/fire-smoke-damage-restoration/): Discuss fire and smoke damage cleanup, affected materials and restoration planning.
- [Mold Remediation](https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/services/mold-remediation/): Discuss mold concerns, cleanup within the published scope and referral for larger or out-of-scope projects.
- [Sewage Backup & Cleanup](https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/services/sewage-backup-cleanup/): Discuss sewage backup cleanup, affected materials and the work needed at the property.
- [Reconstruction & Remodeling](https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/services/construction-remodeling/): Discuss reconstruction and remodeling after cleanup, including the proposed repair scope and scheduling.

## Documented Texas projects

- [Arlington bathroom mold remediation](https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/projects/arlington-bathroom-mold-remediation/): Completed August 2026. The water-supply line serving the sink was the source of the leak. This project involved the bathroom wall, so the work went beyond cleaning a spot on a visible surface. Our team reports that the mold had been removed and the bathroom was ready for reconstruction when the cleanup was finished. Reconstruction was the next step, rather than part of the completed work shown here. No independent clearance result is included in this account.
- [Dallas kitchen and laundry mold remediation](https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/projects/dallas-kitchen-laundry-mold-remediation/): Completed September 2026. In the kitchen, the leak came from the P-trap, the curved section of drainpipe below the sink. In the laundry area, water was leaking at the supply connections. Both areas were part of the remediation project. Our team reports that the mold was removed and that the project passed testing by an independent mold consultant and laboratory. The testing reports are not included in this project account.

## Planning a project

Describe the affected rooms, known water source, when the problem was noticed and whether a plumber or other contractor has already attended. Share any existing assessment report. Ask what containment, removal, disposal, monitoring and rebuilding the estimate includes, and who is responsible for each stage. Do not use a photo or another project’s outcome to determine the scope or clearance status of a different property.

## Project accounts and evidence

### Arlington bathroom mold remediation

A leak in the bathroom sink’s water-supply line led to mold at this Arlington property. Our team contained the bathroom, removed affected wall material and cleaned the work area. The project was completed in August 2026, leaving the bathroom ready for reconstruction.

We contained the bathroom before demolishing the affected wall and removing mold-affected material. We then cleaned the work area using remediation procedures and equipment. The photos show the doorway containment, equipment and the opened wall around the plumbing.

Our team reports that the mold had been removed and the bathroom was ready for reconstruction when the cleanup was finished. Reconstruction was the next step, rather than part of the completed work shown here. No independent clearance result is included in this account.

[Read the project and view its photographs](https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/projects/arlington-bathroom-mold-remediation/). Project details and outcomes were supplied by the company; customer addresses are omitted.

### Dallas kitchen and laundry mold remediation

This Dallas project involved mold in two parts of the home: the kitchen and the laundry area. A leaking P-trap under the kitchen sink and leaking laundry water connections were the sources of the problem. Our team completed the remediation work in September 2026.

We contained the affected space before proceeding with demolition and mold removal. The work included removing mold-affected materials and using remediation equipment during cleanup. The kitchen photos below show the containment, opened walls and equipment in the work area.

Our team reports that the mold was removed and that the project passed testing by an independent mold consultant and laboratory. The testing reports are not included in this project account.

[Read the project and view its photographs](https://gogreenrestorationtx.com/projects/dallas-kitchen-laundry-mold-remediation/). Project details and outcomes were supplied by the company; customer addresses are omitted.
